subject: Private offer: discount stacking & reseller traceability
messages:

Subject: Private offer questions: discount stacking + reseller fees

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement has a couple of specific asks before we proceed with the PO and Marketplace private offer:

1) Can Redwood support stacking of a non‑marketplace customer discount (a negotiated entrenched price) on top of a marketplace private offer list price? If so, how is that represented on the invoice and in the marketplace settlement?

2) CloudCorps uses ResellCo as our channel partner for North America. We need confirmation of the reseller pass‑through: will ResellCo receive a single consolidated commission from Redwood, or will the commission routing be done via marketplace passback (i.e., separate settlement on AWS/GCP)? We need the audit trail for our finance team.

3) Please provide a simple channel margin worksheet and a redline of the PO showing where discounts are applied (customer net vs marketplace net).

We'd like to close the commercial terms this week if possible — procurement is ready to issue a draft PO pending answers.

Attachments: CloudCorps_RFP.pdf (1.2MB)

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Procurement, CloudCorps
procurement@cloudcorps.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Private offer questions: discount stacking + reseller fees

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: yes we can support a customer‑level discount on top of a private offer list price, and we can provide a per‑invoice audit trail for reseller commission routing. See details below and an attached workbook that outlines the passback flow.

Quick summary:
- Discount stacking: Redwood's private offer model lets you set a marketplace list price and then apply a negotiated customer discount at the contract level. The invoice will show the marketplace list price, the customer discount line, and the net paid by the customer.
- Reseller settlement: we support both (a) Redwood pays ResellCo directly as a partner payout outside the marketplace, or (b) marketplace passback using the cloud provider's settlement mechanism. Option (b) is supported for AWS and GCP but has longer reconciliation windows.

I attached Channel_Split_Workbook.xlsx with two tabs: "Customer View" (what CloudCorps sees on invoice) and "Channel Ops" (how ResellCo is paid).

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm whether CloudCorps prefers Redwood->ResellCo direct payout, or marketplace passback.
2) If direct payout, confirm payment terms and PO contact.
3) If passback, we'll loop in our Marketplace Ops and provide settlement timing and example settlements.

I'm free for a 30m call this afternoon if you want to go line by line.

Attachments: Channel_Split_Workbook.xlsx (12KB)

— Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private offer questions: discount stacking + reseller fees

Elena — tagging in the channel ops details you requested. Inline answers below.

>> Can Redwood support stacking of a non‑marketplace customer discount on top of a marketplace private offer list price?
Yes. Practical notes: the marketplace list price remains the "reference" in the provider console. The customer discount is applied via our contract management layer and is reflected in the invoice as a line item. For accounting teams that require a single net line, we can provide a contracted net price in the PO and additional invoice annotations for audit.

>> How is reseller commission routed and audited?
Option A — Direct Redwood payout to ResellCo (recommended for speed): Redwood issues partner payouts monthly into ResellCo's partner account. Settlement evidence: payout remittance report + a CSV export.
Option B — Marketplace passback (AWS/GCP): cloud provider processes the passback; Redwood can ingest the provider settlement report, map settlement IDs back to the customer invoice, and provide a reconciliation CSV. This path requires 1–2 full billing cycles for complete reconciliation.

Simple margin example (shown in Channel_Split_Workbook.xlsx tab "Channel Ops"):
- Marketplace list: $100,000
- Customer discount: 20% => customer pays $80,000
- Reseller commission: 15% of customer net => $12,000 to ResellCo
- Redwood net recognized: $68,000

If you want the commission treated against list price instead we can model that; we've included both in the workbook.

Attachments in this thread: Channel_Split_Workbook.xlsx (see tab examples).

Ben Carter
Head of Channel Sales, Redwood Inference
